run.answer: The Day 2 exercises for the 3-day full-body program are: Trap-bar or kettlebell deadlift (3 sets of 5 to 8), Dumbbell overhead press (3 sets of 6 to 10), Lat pulldown (3 sets of 8 to 12), Reverse lunge (2 to 3 sets of 8 to 10 each side), and Dead bug (2 to 3 sets) [1].

run.answer: To progress toward strict bodyweight pull-ups, you can use several intermediate steps that preserve the movement pattern, such as slow eccentrics, band-assisted pull-ups, machine-assisted pull-ups, isometric holds, and scapular pull-ups [1].

run.answer: If the bar stalls above the knee and climbs in stages during lockout, it likely indicates that you lost position earlier in the lift [1]. To help address this, you can use variations such as paused deadlifts, RDLs, and block pulls, depending on where the breakdown occurs [1].

- Suitcase carry: 2 to 4 trips per side [1]
sources: 15-core-training-and-posture.md > Core Training, Bracing, and Posture Without the Myths > Better advice for desk workers

run.answer: A complete warm-up can be done in ten to fifteen minutes [1]. A practical formula for this duration is: 3 to 5 minutes of general movement, 3 to 5 minutes of targeted mobility or activation, and 5 to 10 minutes of progressively specific sets [1].

run.answer: The following rep ranges are used for specific roles: 1 to 3 reps for high specificity [1], 3 to 6 reps for repeated strength practice [1], and 6 to 12 or more reps for assistance [1].

run.answer: An active adult should aim for approximately 1.6 to 2.2 grams of protein per kilogram of body weight daily [1]. For better digestion and use, as well as appetite control, it is often easier to spread protein intake across three to five meals rather than consuming one large serving [2].

For demanding sets, resting between two to five minutes is common and often useful [1]. The movement you care about most should be placed early in the session [1].
sources: 05-strength-programming-basics.md > Strength Programming Basics > Rest periods and session order

run.answer: Weekly volume is likely appropriate if you experience steady progress in load or reps, soreness that disappears between sessions, stable technique on later sets, and the target muscle feels challenged [1]. Conversely, volume may be too high if performance decreases and soreness persists throughout the week [1].
sources: 06-hypertrophy-training.md > Hypertrophy Training > Sets per week and dosing volume

run.answer: Red flags for accumulated fatigue or overtraining include a persistent drop in performance, unusual fatigue that rest days cannot resolve, and sleep disruption despite exhaustion [1]. Other signs include frequent minor illness, low mood, flat motivation, or unusual training anxiety, as well as an elevated resting heart rate or a sense of lagging recovery [1]. Additionally, warning signs that recovery is slipping include irritability, stubborn soreness, reduced coordination, and needing much higher effort to reach normal training numbers [3].
sources: 07-sleep-and-recovery.md > Sleep and Recovery for Training Progress > Hard Training, Overreaching, and Overtraining
07-sleep-and-recovery.md > Sleep and Recovery for Training Progress > Practical Recovery Signals to Watch

run.answer: The practical shortlist for many recreational lifters includes creatine monohydrate (for strength or muscle gain), caffeine (if tolerated and timed intelligently), and protein powder (to help meet protein intake goals) [3]. Vitamin D is included only when supported by clinical guidance or personal context [3].
sources: 17-supplements-and-ergogenic-aids.md > Supplements and Ergogenic Aids: What Helps, What Does Not, and How to Use Them Safely > A practical shortlist

run.answer: A smart return to training follows a five-step logic: 1) reduce the load that aggravates the irritated tissue [1]; 2) continue training what can be done safely [1]; 3) rebuild tolerance and local strength [1]; 4) gradually reintroduce loading specific to lifting or sport [1]; and 5) progress based on how symptoms respond rather than ego [1].
sources: 11-injury-prevention-and-rehab.md > Injury Prevention and Rehab for People Who Train > Return to Training: Modify, Do Not Guess

run.answer: To reduce interference when strength is your main goal, you should prioritize zone 2 modalities with low eccentric stress, such as incline walking or cycling, rather than frequent hard runs [1]. Additionally, you can reduce conflict by keeping most cardio easy, separating hard cardio sessions from hard lifting sessions whenever possible, prioritizing the quality of sessions most important to your goal, and ensuring appropriate fueling, particularly with carbohydrates around demanding work [1].
sources: 12-cardio-and-conditioning.md > Cardio and Conditioning for Strength, Health, and Work Capacity > Concurrent Training: Mixing Cardio and Strength

run.answer:
Workout B of the sample full-body home training week consists of the following exercises: [4]

*   Split squat: 3 sets of 8 to 12 each side [4]
*   Standing dumbbell overhead press: 3 sets of 6 to 10 [4]
*   Band row or pulldown: 3 sets of 10 to 15 [4]
*   Hip thrust or glute bridge: 3 sets of 10 to 15 [4]
*   Pallof press or suitcase carry: 2 to 3 sets [4]
sources: 14-home-workouts-and-bodyweight.md > Home Workouts with Dumbbells, Bands, and Bodyweight > Workout B

run.answer: Instead of seeking a flawless position, desk workers should aim for support and variability [2]. Practical strategies include alternating between upright and relaxed positions, standing up, walking, or changing posture regularly [2]. Additionally, you should use training to increase tolerance rather than attempting to freeze in a single shape [2].
sources: 15-core-training-and-posture.md > Core Training, Bracing, and Posture Without the Myths > Better advice for desk workers

run.answer: A useful rule is to never miss twice when it is avoidable [1]. Instead of self-criticism, the recommended follow-up action is to resume your next available session, such as Tuesday or Wednesday, and return to your normal schedule to maintain momentum, rather than trying to make up every missed workout [1].
sources: 16-motivation-habits-and-consistency.md > Motivation, Habits, and Consistency in Fitness > Dealing with missed sessions

run.answer: A simple bench press setup checklist before unracking includes: planting and keeping feet still, keeping glutes on the bench, ensuring the upper back is tight against the pad, setting the shoulder blades before the unrack, and placing hands evenly on the bar [1].
sources: 03-bench-press-and-pushing.md > Bench Press and Pushing > Bench press setup

run.answer: A balanced weekly plan for back training should include at least one vertical pull, at least one row, some work for the rear-delts or face-pulls, and sufficient total volume to allow for progress without causing elbow inflammation [1].
sources: 04-pulling-and-back-training.md > Pulling and Back Training > Organizing back training

run.answer: In high-bar positioning, the bar rests on the upper traps, which typically allows for more knee travel and a more upright torso [1]. In contrast, the low-bar position places the bar lower across the rear delts, often allowing for more load but requiring more torso lean and a firmer upper-back shelf [2].
sources: 01-squat-technique.md > Barbell Back Squat Technique
01-squat-technique.md > Barbell Back Squat Technique > Rack setup and bar position > Low-bar

run.answer: Если тренировки частые или требовательные, то перед тренировкой рекомендуется принимать пищу, содержащую углеводы и немного белка, за один-три часа до занятия [1]. После тренировки вполне разумно употребить белок и немного углеводов в течение нескольких часов после завершения [1].
sources: 08-nutrition-protein-and-calories.md > Nutrition, Protein, and Calories for Fitness Goals > How to Set Macros Without Overcomplicating It

run.answer: Если кажется, что наступило плато, сначала проверьте: была ли последовательной приверженность плану, действительно ли средний вес стоит несколько недель, не снизилась ли активность вне тренировок и нет ли причин для задержки воды [1]. Если плато реально, обычные исправления включают: небольшое снижение калорий, увеличение ежедневной активности, повышение точности порций и улучшение стабильности в выходные дни [1].

В программу Lower B для 4-дневного сплита входят следующие упражнения:

- Вариация становой тяги (Deadlift variation): 3 подхода по 5–6 повторений [1].
- Фронтальные, гоблет-приседания или хак-приседания (Front squat, goblet squat, or hack squat): 3 подхода по 8–10 повторений [1].
- Ягодичный мостик или сгибание ног (Hip thrust or leg curl): 2–3 подхода [1].
- Зашагивания или выпады при ходьбе (Step-up or walking lunge): 2 подхода на каждую сторону [1].
- Жим Паллофа или переноска (Pallof press or carry): 2–3 подхода [1].
sources: 13-beginner-program-design.md > Beginner Program Design for Strength and Muscle > A practical 4-day upper/lower split

run.answer: В конце руководства перечислены следующие полезные подсказки (cues) для тяги: заклините себя под штангой (wedge yourself to the bar), прижмите штангу к ногам (squeeze the bar to the legs), отталкивайтесь от пола (push the floor away), держите подмышки напряженными (keep the armpits tight) и стойте прямо, не отклоняясь назад (stand tall, do not lean back) [1].
sources: 02-deadlift-technique.md > Deadlift Technique > Common deadlift faults and fixes > Bent arms

run.answer:
Протеиновый порошок наиболее полезен в следующих случаях: [1]
- когда трудно достичь суточной нормы белка только с помощью обычной еды; [1]
- когда требуется быстрый вариант питания во время работы или поездок; [1]
- когда аппетит снижен в периоды тяжелых тренировок; [1]
- когда жидкий вариант просто более практичен, чем полноценный прием пищи. [1]
Также порошок может быть очень полезен, если работа, аппетит или график затрудняют потребление белка. [2]

For demanding sets, resting between two to five minutes is common and often useful [1]. The movement you care about most should be placed early in the session [1].
sources: 05-strength-programming-basics.md > Strength Programming Basics > Rest periods and session order

run.answer: Weekly volume is likely appropriate if you experience steady progress in load or reps, soreness that disappears between sessions, stable technique on later sets, and the target muscle feels challenged [1]. Conversely, volume may be too high if performance decreases and soreness persists throughout the week [1].
sources: 06-hypertrophy-training.md > Hypertrophy Training > Sets per week and dosing volume

run.answer: Red flags for accumulated fatigue or overtraining include a persistent drop in performance, unusual fatigue that rest days cannot resolve, and sleep disruption despite exhaustion [1]. Other signs include frequent minor illness, low mood, flat motivation, or unusual training anxiety, as well as an elevated resting heart rate or a sense of lagging recovery [1]. Additionally, warning signs that recovery is slipping include irritability, stubborn soreness, reduced coordination, and needing much higher effort to reach normal training numbers [3].
sources: 07-sleep-and-recovery.md > Sleep and Recovery for Training Progress > Hard Training, Overreaching, and Overtraining
07-sleep-and-recovery.md > Sleep and Recovery for Training Progress > Practical Recovery Signals to Watch

run.answer: The practical shortlist for many recreational lifters includes creatine monohydrate (for strength or muscle gain), caffeine (if tolerated and timed intelligently), and protein powder (to help meet protein intake goals) [3]. Vitamin D is included only when supported by clinical guidance or personal context [3].
sources: 17-supplements-and-ergogenic-aids.md > Supplements and Ergogenic Aids: What Helps, What Does Not, and How to Use Them Safely > A practical shortlist

run.answer: A smart return to training follows a five-step logic: 1) reduce the load that aggravates the irritated tissue [1]; 2) continue training what can be done safely [1]; 3) rebuild tolerance and local strength [1]; 4) gradually reintroduce loading specific to lifting or sport [1]; and 5) progress based on your symptoms rather than ego [1].
sources: 11-injury-prevention-and-rehab.md > Injury Prevention and Rehab for People Who Train > Return to Training: Modify, Do Not Guess

run.answer: To reduce interference when strength is your main goal, you should prioritize zone 2 modalities with low eccentric stress, such as incline walking or cycling, rather than frequent hard runs [1]. Additionally, you can reduce conflict by keeping most cardio easy, separating hard cardio sessions from hard lifting sessions whenever possible, prioritizing the quality of sessions most important to your goal, and ensuring appropriate fueling, particularly with carbohydrates around demanding work [1].
sources: 12-cardio-and-conditioning.md > Cardio and Conditioning for Strength, Health, and Work Capacity > Concurrent Training: Mixing Cardio and Strength

run.answer:
Workout B of the sample full-body home training week consists of the following exercises: [4]

*   Split squat: 3 sets of 8 to 12 each side [4]
*   Standing dumbbell overhead press: 3 sets of 6 to 10 [4]
*   Band row or pulldown: 3 sets of 10 to 15 [4]
*   Hip thrust or glute bridge: 3 sets of 10 to 15 [4]
*   Pallof press or suitcase carry: 2 to 3 sets [4]
sources: 14-home-workouts-and-bodyweight.md > Home Workouts with Dumbbells, Bands, and Bodyweight > Workout B

run.answer: Instead of seeking a flawless position, desk workers should aim for support and variability [2]. Practical strategies include alternating between upright and relaxed positions, standing up, walking, or changing posture regularly [2]. Additionally, you should use training to increase tolerance rather than attempting to freeze in a single shape [2].
sources: 15-core-training-and-posture.md > Core Training, Bracing, and Posture Without the Myths > Better advice for desk workers

run.answer: A useful rule is to never miss twice when it is avoidable [1]. Instead of self-criticism, the recommended follow-up action is to resume your next available session, such as Tuesday or Wednesday, and return to your normal schedule to maintain momentum, rather than trying to make up every missed workout [1].
sources: 16-motivation-habits-and-consistency.md > Motivation, Habits, and Consistency in Fitness > Dealing with missed sessions

run.answer: A simple bench press setup checklist before unracking includes: planting and keeping feet still, keeping glutes on the bench, ensuring the upper back is tight against the pad, setting the shoulder blades before the unrack, and placing hands evenly on the bar [1].
sources: 03-bench-press-and-pushing.md > Bench Press and Pushing > Bench press setup

run.answer: A balanced weekly plan for back training should include at least one vertical pull, at least one row, some work for the rear-delts or face-pulls, and sufficient total volume to allow for progress without causing elbow inflammation [1].
sources: 04-pulling-and-back-training.md > Pulling and Back Training > Organizing back training

run.answer: In high-bar positioning, the bar rests on the upper traps, which typically allows for more knee travel and a more upright torso [1]. In contrast, the low-bar position places the bar lower across the rear delts, often allowing for more load but requiring more torso lean and a firmer upper-back shelf [2].
sources: 01-squat-technique.md > Barbell Back Squat Technique
01-squat-technique.md > Barbell Back Squat Technique > Rack setup and bar position > Low-bar

run.answer: Если тренировки частые или требовательные, то перед тренировкой рекомендуется принимать пищу, содержащую углеводы и немного белка, за один-три часа до занятия [1]. После тренировки вполне разумно употребить белок и немного углеводов в течение нескольких часов после завершения [1].
sources: 08-nutrition-protein-and-calories.md > Nutrition, Protein, and Calories for Fitness Goals > How to Set Macros Without Overcomplicating It

run.answer: Если кажется, что наступило плато, сначала проверьте следующее: была ли последовательной приверженность плану, действительно ли средний вес не меняется в течение нескольких недель, не снизилась ли активность вне тренировок и нет ли причин для задержки воды [1]. Если плато реально, обычные исправления включают: небольшое снижение калорий, увеличение ежедневной активности, повышение точности порций и улучшение стабильности в выходные дни [1].
sources: 09-fat-loss-and-body-composition.md > Fat Loss and Body Composition Without Losing the Plot > Tracking Intake and Progress > Measurements and photos

В программу Lower B для 4-дневного сплита входят следующие упражнения:

- Вариация становой тяги (Deadlift variation): 3 подхода по 5–6 повторений [1].
- Фронтальные, гоблет-приседания или хак-приседания (Front squat, goblet squat, or hack squat): 3 подхода по 8–10 повторений [1].
- Ягодичный мостик или сгибание ног (Hip thrust or leg curl): 2–3 подхода [1].
- Зашагивания или выпады при ходьбе (Step-up or walking lunge): 2 подхода на каждую сторону [1].
- Пресс Паллофа или переноска (Pallof press or carry): 2–3 подхода [1].
sources: 13-beginner-program-design.md > Beginner Program Design for Strength and Muscle > A practical 4-day upper/lower split

run.answer: В конце руководства перечислены следующие полезные подсказки (cues) для тяги: заклините себя под штангой (wedge yourself to the bar), прижмите штангу к ногам (squeeze the bar to the legs), отталкивайтесь от пола (push the floor away), держите подмышки напряженными (keep the armpits tight) и стойте прямо, не отклоняясь назад (stand tall, do not lean back) [1].
sources: 02-deadlift-technique.md > Deadlift Technique > Common deadlift faults and fixes > Bent arms

run.answer:
Протеиновый порошок наиболее полезен в следующих случаях: [1]
- когда трудно достичь суточной нормы белка только с помощью обычной еды; [1]
- когда требуется быстрый вариант питания во время работы или поездок; [1]
- когда аппетит снижен в периоды тяжелых тренировок; [1]
- когда жидкий вариант просто более практичен, чем полноценный прием пищи. [1]
Также порошок может быть очень полезен, если работа, аппетит или график затрудняют потребление белка. [2]
sources: 17-supplements-and-ergogenic-aids.md > Supplements and Ergogenic Aids: What Helps, What Does Not, and How to Use Them Safely > Protein powder > When powder earns its place

run.answer: Для безопасного прогресса новичкам рекомендуется использовать интервалы бега и ходьбы, если это необходимо [1], постепенно увеличивать общий объем [1] и придерживаться умеренного темпа в большинстве тренировок [1]. Важно избегать одновременного увеличения дистанции и интенсивности [1], а также не превращать каждую пробежку в проверку своих возможностей [1].
